solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flee Daleks regrouping over two days near Earth

indicators.note: near says the next piece comes right beside the previous ones
the rearranged letters sit over, covering on both sides, the two days
regrouping says the Daleks are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for day, so two of them give DD

explanation.surface: Doctor Who's Daleks scatter and regroup after a couple of days in orbit close to Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering: the shuffled alien name wraps around the two days rather than sitting above them.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is an informal verb for running away hastily, a synonym of flee.

clue.text: One keeping items stuck in a corner

definitions.text: One keeping items stuck in a corner

parts.words: One keeping items stuck in a corner
parts.note: a philatelist keeps small gummed items, fixed in albums by hinges or mounts in the corner of each one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hoarder cluttering a room's corner; the items are postage stamps, and a stamp is stuck in the corner of an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist hoards postage labels, which are stuck in the top corner of an envelope.

clue.text: Learning game inside publication

indicators.note: inside says the game is placed within the publication

parts.note: an edition is one published issue of a book or paper
RU is the abbreviation for rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone acquires knowledge from a quiz printed in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) goes into EDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is scholarly knowledge gained by study, so a noun for learning.

clue.text: NASA's tour possibly features first of these

definitions.text: NASA's tour possibly features first of these

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could be arranged another way

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored, go into the mix

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of these

parts.note: the word these supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A tour of NASA might well showcase spacefarers first.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NASA'S TOUR plus T, the first letter of 'these', are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer, as a NASA tour shows off its spacefarers.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA's spacefarers would naturally be a highlight of any tour of the space agency.

clue.text: Fiasco of French taxi turning on empty lane

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the piece placed above the next

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: turning says the taxi word runs backwards, up the column in this down clue

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: empty says the inside letters of lane are removed, leaving its outer pair

parts.note: the word lane, emptied to its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A disaster where a French taxi turns onto an empty lane.
explanation.walkthrough: DE, then CAB backwards (BAC), then L and E, the outside of lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating failure, which is what a fiasco is.

clue.text: Theologian contributing to career as musician

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A churchman helps a friend build a life in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Dutch Renaissance scholar and theologian.

clue.text: Apportions pork and turkey maybe verbally

indicators.note: verbally says to go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: pork and turkey are examples of meats

explanation.surface: Someone dishes out portions of roast pork and turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: MEATS sounds identical to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or distribute shares, so metes means apportions.

clue.text: Emperor causing injury having taken aim

indicators.note: having taken says the aim letters are removed from what comes before

parts.note: maiming is causing serious injury

explanation.surface: A ruler hurts people after taking careful aim.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AIM out of MAIMING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ming was a Chinese dynasty whose rulers bore the title emperor; a Ming here stands for one such ruler.

clue.text: Search for capsized vehicle on bottom of lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the next
capsized says the vehicle is turned upside down, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

indicators.note: bottom of takes the last letter, the bottom one in a down light

parts.note: the word lake supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: Divers hunt for an overturned vehicle at the bottom of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: CART upside down gives TRAC; add E, the end of lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace someone is to track them down or find them, a sense of search for.

clue.text: Small spout blocked by child's hooter

indicators.note: blocked by says the child piece goes inside, obstructing the rest

parts.note: a nozzle is a spout
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A small jug spout gets stuck by a child's toy horn.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is British slang for nose, so it is the definition, not a car horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnozzle is a jokey word for a nose, as is hooter in British slang.

clue.text: Bullets regularly on promotion for grown-ups

indicators.note: on puts the next piece after promotion in this across clue

parts.note: an ad is a promotion, an advertisement

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of bullets, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: alternate letters of bullets

explanation.surface: A war film with bullets everywhere is marketed for mature audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (advert) followed by U, L, T from bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult content is restricted to mature audiences, so the adjective means intended for grown-ups.

clue.text: Condition of garment being laundered

parts.note: a bra is a garment
something being laundered is in the wash

explanation.surface: A care label warns about the state of a garment going through the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condition' looks like a noun about the garment's state; it is the verb, as in conditioning minds.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainwash someone is to indoctrinate them, which is a sense of the verb condition.

clue.text: Prince is being filmed with Penny and Nick in wartime

parts.note: someone being filmed is on cam(era)

explanation.surface: A royal is caught on film with a coin and a stolen item during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for prison, so the wartime nick is a camp for prisoners of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A wartime internment site for captured soldiers is a slammer, nick being British slang for jail.

clue.text: Fiddler allegedly caught by Lorenzo in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden run goes backwards
caught by says the letters are held inside the word Lorenzo

parts.note: the name holds the letters, read right to left

explanation.surface: A violinist is said to have been arrested by a man called Lorenzo as he withdrew.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside Lorenzo, OREN read backwards. The legend is that this emperor fiddled while Rome burned, hence 'allegedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor is said to have played music while Rome burned, an alleged fiddler.

clue.text: Plant lawyer to work with corrupt cops

indicators.note: corrupt says the letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: An undercover agent is placed as a lawyer to work alongside bent police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a spy planted among crooked police; it is a flower. The letters of LAWYER and COPS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow parsley is a common white-flowered umbellifer of hedgerows, a wild flower.

clue.text: Cold capital with extremes of the weather

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: extremes of takes the first and last letters of the

explanation.surface: A chilly capital city suffers swings of temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: C, then LIMA, then T and E, the ends of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate is the prevailing pattern of conditions in a region, its usual weather.

clue.text: See 1
Broadcast Naked Spanish Island for Hollywood?

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to show it

indicators.note: naked says the island loses its outer letters, its covering

parts.note: Ibiza is a Spanish island in the Balearics

explanation.surface: A TV channel airs a nude beach programme set on Ibiza, aimed at Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOW plus BIZ, Ibiza stripped of its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood is an example of the entertainment industry, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Soldiers Club cheers on male with pride

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the earlier pieces above the next

parts.note: a bat is a club
ta is British informal for thanks, like cheers
a lion lives in a pride; the male one is called a lion

explanation.surface: Troops at a club toast a proud man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' sounds like vanity; it is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is an army unit made up of several companies of troops.

clue.text: Mr Eastwood originally imported American medicine

indicators.note: the original, opening letter is taken in, imported into the middle of the name

parts.note: Clint Eastwood, the actor

explanation.surface: Clint Eastwood first brought in a cough remedy from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' points at the opening letter of the actor's first name, and 'imported' has it carried into the middle. Linctus is a British word for cough syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a syrupy cough remedy, a type of medicine.

clue.text: Colour ranges son picks left out

indicators.note: out says the left piece is removed from the picks

parts.note: plectra are guitar picks

explanation.surface: A boy chooses paint colours but omits some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picks' looks like a verb; it is the plural noun, plectra.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra are bands of colours, such as those split from white light, so ranges of colour.

clue.text: Calibrated tube or extra-tiny Apple product?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a graduated glass tube for measuring liquids
second meaning: a pip is an apple's seed, and the diminutive -ette makes it an extra-tiny one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple product' suggests an iPhone-style gadget; read it as a seed of the fruit, with -ette shrinking it further.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratories use this graduated glass tube to measure liquid; whimsically it is a mini seed.

clue.text: Bug climbing atop bird model

indicators.note: atop puts the first piece above the bird in the column
climbing says the bug goes upward, read bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: a tap is a bug on a phone line
a tern is a sea bird

explanation.surface: An insect clambers onto a bird figurine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect; it is a phone tap, reversed to PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or template to be copied.

clue.text: Copy husband cloaked in green

indicators.note: cloaked in says the husband is wrapped inside the green word

parts.note: eco is a prefix meaning green, environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: A husband imitates a man dressed in green.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to repeat or imitate, so it means to copy.

clue.text: Hams and wines sourced from Germany

definitions.meaning: first meaning: joints of meat from the leg of a pig
second meaning: hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a German deli selling ham and wine; hock is both the joint and, in British usage, Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock names both a cured pork leg joint and German Rhenish white wine.

clue.text: Drink with gambler's spouse

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler
a half is a half-pint of beer in a British pub

explanation.surface: A punter's wife joins him for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A half is a half-pint, the usual British pub order.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is a jocular idiom for one's wife or husband.

clue.text: Cheat periodically using faux degree

indicators.note: periodically takes the letters at regular intervals: first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A fraudster occasionally relies on a fake qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: To fudge results is to fake or falsify them, a sense of cheat.

clue.text: Virgin territory confiscated from state

indicators.note: confiscated from says the territory is taken away from the state

parts.note: Maryland is a US state
land is territory

explanation.surface: Unspoiled land is seized by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin territory' looks like a phrase; 'Virgin' alone is the definition, the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary, mother of Jesus, is called the Virgin in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Note play on court one, vacated for Yankee game

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the play after the court

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
an act is a part of a play, or to play

indicators.note: vacated says one is emptied of its middle letter, leaving its ends

parts.note: the word one with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A musician plays tennis on court one, which is then cleared for an American game.
explanation.walkthrough: TI, CT, ACT, and O and E from one. Yankee here means American: this is the US name for noughts and crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tic-tac-toe is the American name for the grid game noughts and crosses.

clue.text: Isle acquired by fat landowner

indicators.note: acquired by says the isle is taken into the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A wealthy owner of property buys an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Dangerous knights returned with one of the axes

indicators.note: returned says the knights are read backwards

parts.note: two knights: K, the chess knight, and SIR, a knight's title
y is one of the axes on a graph

explanation.surface: Knights coming back carrying battle-axes are a perilous sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' suggests weapons; it is the plural of axis, as on a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky carries the chance of harm, so is hazardous.

clue.text: Wild north ocean overcoming tug briefly in bother

indicators.note: overcoming says the rearranged letters sit over the tug, enclosing it
wild says the letters run free in a new order
briefly says the tug word loses its last letter

parts.note: to yank is to tug

explanation.surface: A rough northern ocean overpowers a small tug, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tug' looks like a boat on the ocean; it is the verb yank, cut short by 'briefly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance is irritation or vexation, a noun sense of bother.
